name: Deserted Workshop
summary: Tucked against the dunes northwest of Gadgetzan, the Deserted Workshop is an enigmatic crash site nestled along the border mountains. Marked by skid tracks descending from Thousand Needles and a wrecked rocket car embedded in the hillside, it stands as a silent testament to a high-speed technological disaster.

sections.title: A High-Velocity Blunder
sections.body: Just northwest of the bustling goblin trading post of Gadgetzan lies a lonely hillside littered with scorched metal and scrap. At the center of the wreckage rests a shattered rocket car, its frame crushed against the rocky incline. Deep skid tracks trace its erratic journey from high in the northern mountains dividing Tanaris and Thousand Needles. While the site sits abandoned and offers no obvious clues to the driver's fate, its design is unmistakable to anyone familiar with the intense vehicle trials across the ridge.

sections.title: Echoes of the Salt Flats
sections.body: The crashed racer matches the high-strung, volatile drag carts built and tested on the Mirage Raceway down in the Shimmering Flats. It seems an intrepid—or reckless—engineer managed to launch their contraption straight through the mountain pass, ending a disastrous test run in the sands of Tanaris. With no survivor in sight, the desert winds slowly bury the wreckage beside the dusty ridges.

faq.q: What is the wrecked vehicle embedded in the hill?
faq.answer: It is a wrecked rocket car, identical to the volatile racing vehicles engineered for high-speed trials on the nearby salt flats. Judging by the skid marks leading down from the ridge, a driver lost control high in the mountains and crashed hard into the Tanaris hillside.

faq.q: Where did the crashed car come from?
faq.answer: The tread marks and gouges in the rock trace northward into the steep mountains bordering Thousand Needles. It almost certainly originated from the Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats, where gnomes and goblins constantly test reckless rocket-propulsion prototypes.

faq.q: Who was driving the rocket car?
faq.answer: The driver's identity remains unknown, and no body or survivor lingers at the crash site. Whether they were recovered, managed to limp away back to Gadgetzan, or perished to the local scavengers is left entirely to mystery.

faq.q: Why is the area called the Deserted Workshop?
faq.answer: Despite the name, there is no formal workshop building standing here—only the shattered remains of an engineering endeavor and abandoned tools scattered across the sands.

angles.text: Every engineer who spots the crash site immediately recognizes the hallmark risks of experimental rocket fuel and overpowered thrusters pushing chassis far beyond safe tolerances.
Looking at the catastrophic collision, any gnomish tinkerer would suspect either reckless goblin corner-cutting or a wildly ambitious high-speed record attempt gone wrong.
